profile.summary: FramePool predicts how strongly a 5' untranslated region (5' UTR) drives translation, measured as mean ribosome load, directly from the 5' UTR sequence. It is a convolutional network trained on a massively parallel reporter assay, made to accept 5' UTRs of any length by pooling motif detections separately in each of the three reading frames. Through Kipoi, it takes variants from a VCF file and reports the predicted log2 fold change in mean ribosome load for each affected 5' UTR.

summary_quotes.text: Recently, a model was trained on a massively parallel reporter assay to predict mean ribosome load (MRL)
Here, we introduced frame pooling, a novel neural network operation that enabled the development of an MRL prediction model for 5’UTRs of any length.
we perform these pooling operations on each frame seperately
This model predicts the log2 fold change in mean ribosome load from introducing variants

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: FramePool adapts the published MPRA model of Sample et al. That model used a dense layer, so it only worked for the sequence lengths it was trained on. FramePool keeps three convolutional layers (kernel size 7, 128 filters each, with residual skip connections) and replaces the position-specific dense input with global max and average pooling, done separately for each of the three frames relative to the start codon. The pooled values (a vector of 768) go into a dense layer of 64 neurons and a final linear output. Each model has 282,625 learnable weights; the combined model has 4 more in a scaling layer. The model was trained with the Adam optimiser and a mean squared error loss.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The paper trains three models: FramePool50 on 50-nucleotide MPRA sequences, FramePool100 on 25 to 100 nucleotide sequences, and FramePoolCombined on both, with a scaling layer for the two libraries. The paper names FramePoolCombined as the model for variant effect prediction from VCF files. The Kipoi zoo entry downloads the weights file Framepool_combined_residual.h5 from Zenodo record 3584238 with a fixed md5 checksum. A result should name the Kipoi model (Framepool), the weights checksum and the kipoi/models commit; this page read commit 770dcaf2.

facts.value: Supervised convolutional neural network regression model predicting mean ribosome load from 5' UTR sequence, with a variant effect interface in Kipoi.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Three convolutional layers (kernel size 7, 128 filters, residual skip connections, ReLU), frame pooling (global max and average pooling per reading frame, giving a vector of 768), a dense layer of 64 neurons with dropout 0.2, and a linear output. Implemented in Keras with a TensorFlow backend.

quotes.text: The three convolutional layers all have a kernel size of 7 and 128 filters each. The dense layer has 64 neurons and a dropout with a drop-rate of 0.2 is applied to its outputs.
Global max pooling will return three tensors of shape (128,), and so will global average pooling. After concatenation, a tensor of shape (768,) remains.
The model was implemented using Keras with a Tensorflow backend.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: MPRA data from Sample et al. on an eGFP library in HEK293T cells: 260,000 random 50-nucleotide 5' UTRs with mean ribosome load (20,000 held out for validation), and 76,319 random 5' UTRs of 25 to 100 nucleotides. FramePoolCombined used both training sets.

facts.label: Training cutoff
facts.value: Not reported. The model was trained on a fixed published MPRA dataset (Sample et al.), and the paper gives no data collection date.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: No fixed length: frame pooling lets the model take 5' UTRs of any length. The paper notes that upstream open reading frames longer than the receptive field, 19 nucleotides, cannot be reliably detected.

In our architecture, this limits uORF that can reliably be detected to a length of 19 nt.

run_guide.summary: Install Kipoi, create the Framepool environment, and score the example variants with the Kipoi command line, as shown on the Kipoi model page.
prerequisites: conda (anaconda or miniconda), which Kipoi uses to manage model dependencies. Kipoi maintains Python 3.6 to 3.10.
For Python 3.8 to 3.10, the Kipoi README says hdf5 and pkgconfig must be installed before Kipoi.
The Framepool environment itself pins Python 3.7, TensorFlow 1.13.1 and Keras 2.2.4. A GPU is not mentioned.
Code and weights are MIT licensed.

steps.title: Install Kipoi
steps.explanation: The Kipoi README install command. It installs the latest Kipoi release, not a pinned version.

quotes.text: Kipoi requires [conda](https://conda.io/) to manage model dependencies.
pip install kipoi

steps.title: Create and activate the Framepool environment
steps.shell:
kipoi env create Framepool
source activate kipoi-Framepool
steps.explanation: Creates a conda environment with the dependencies from the Framepool model definition and activates it.

steps.title: Score the example variants
steps.shell:
kipoi get-example Framepool -o example
kipoi predict Framepool \
  --dataloader_args='{"intervals_file": "example/intervals_file", "fasta_file": "example/fasta_file", "vcf_file": "example/vcf_file", "vcf_file_tbi": "example/vcf_file_tbi", "chr_order_file": "example/chr_order_file", "num_chr": true}' \
  -o '/tmp/Framepool.example_pred.tsv'
# check the results
head '/tmp/Framepool.example_pred.tsv'
steps.explanation: The Kipoi page's prediction commands, with HTML entities decoded. They download the example BED, FASTA and VCF files, run the model on them and show the first lines of the output table.

limitations: These commands were read from the Kipoi page and README and have not been executed by Rewire.
The Kipoi README notes h5py compatibility issues for models saved with h5py below version 3; the Framepool environment pins h5py 2.9.0.
To retrain or reproduce the paper, the README points to the Model_Training.ipynb notebook and the Zenodo data instead; that route is not covered here.

notes: The source paper (key paper) is the same article as the existing source uc20260930-source-framepool-2021, fetched here from the publisher as JATS XML so it could be quoted. The 5UTR repository's own kipoi/5UTR_Model/model.yaml differs from the kipoi/models zoo version (it loads a bundled .h5 file and has a single seq input); this page follows the zoo version. Statements quoting the Kipoi page match its raw HTML, so quotes contain HTML entities.
